easy.explain: Khadijah died about five years before Badr, in the Year of Sorrow.
Umar accepted Islam during the Makkan persecution, about fourteen years before Makkah was entered.
Six years separate Uhud from Tabuk, the last expedition the Prophet ﷺ led in person.
About twenty-six years separate the first revelation from the decisive battle in Syria under Umar.
Four years separate the truce at Hudaybiyyah from the Farewell Pilgrimage.

events.text: The caliphate of Abu Bakr begins

easy.explain: Twenty-four years and two caliphates separate the first and fourth of the Rashidun.
Three years separate the siege of Madinah from Hunayn, fought just after the conquest of Makkah.
About eleven years separate the start of the public call from the first major battle.

events.text: The passing of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: Al-Bukhari compiled his collection more than two centuries after the Prophet's passing.
More than five centuries separate the founder of the Maliki school from Ibn Taymiyyah.
The five daily prayers were prescribed at the Mi'raj, before the Hijrah; the qiblah changed afterwards, in Madinah.

events.text: The standardisation of the Qur'an under Uthman

easy.explain: The losses at Yamamah prompted the first written compilation; the standardisation of copies came more than a decade later.
About twenty-seven years separate the marriage from the migration.

events.text: The martyrdom of Husayn at Karbala

easy.explain: Fifty-three years separate Mu'tah, in the Prophet's lifetime, from Karbala.
Eighteen years and two caliphates separate Uthman's accession from the beginning of Umayyad rule.

medium.explain: The night journey came late in the Makkan period, roughly a decade after the first revelation and two years before the migration.
Surah Al-Hashr relates to the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir, which fell between Badr and the siege at Khandaq.
The siege of Ta'if followed Hunayn in the same year as the conquest, with Tabuk the following year.
Yamamah under Abu Bakr, then Yarmuk against the Byzantines and Nahawand against the Sasanians under Umar.
Uthman's twelve-year caliphate, then Ali's, then the establishment of Umayyad rule in 41 AH.
Ahmad ibn Hanbal studied under al-Shafi'i, and al-Bukhari belongs to the generation after him.
The last of the six compilers, then al-Tabari within a decade, then al-Ghazali nearly two centuries later.
Sixty years from birth to the peaceful conquest of the city he had been driven from.
The pledge, then the migration the following year, then Badr two years after that.

events.text: The martyrdom of Husayn at Karbala
The caliphate of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz

medium.explain: Karbala, then the brief and widely praised caliphate of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, then the fall of the Umayyads.
Fasting was legislated early in Madinah; Hajj later, commonly given as 9 AH, with the Prophet performing it the following year.
The postponed Umrah in 7 AH, then two engagements within 8 AH, Mu'tah before the conquest and Hunayn after it.
The loss of his protector was followed by the rejection at Ta'if and then by the pledge from the people of Yathrib.
The constitution on arrival, the change of qiblah the following year, and the truce with the Quraysh four years after that.
Two major events of Umar's caliphate, followed by Uthman's accession in 23 AH.

hard.explain: Twenty years from the marriage to Khadijah to the first flight from persecution.

events.text: The boycott of Banu Hashim begins
Khadijah and Abu Talib pass away

hard.explain: The hardest stretch of the Makkan period. Several of these dates are approximate and sources differ over their exact sequence.
The first five years in Madinah, one major event per year.
The two years following the truce, in which Khaybar was taken, the postponed Umrah performed, and Makkah finally entered.
The final two years of the Prophet's life, from Hunayn through to the Farewell Pilgrimage.

events.text: The passing of the Prophet ﷺ
The compilation of the Qur'an under Abu Bakr

hard.explain: Abu Bakr's entire caliphate, from the Prophet's passing to Umar's accession two years later.
Umar's caliphate in sequence. The taking of Jerusalem and the institution of the calendar fall very close together.

events.text: The caliphate of Hasan ibn Ali

hard.explain: From the standardisation of the mushaf under Uthman through the first fitnah to the end of the Rashidun period.

events.text: The martyrdom of Husayn at Karbala
The caliphate of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz

hard.explain: From the founding of Umayyad rule to the death of Malik ibn Anas, well into the Abbasid period.
The same sequence as before, given in Hijri years rather than Common Era.
Five of the six compilers in Hijri years. Ibn Majah, who died in 273 AH, falls between Muslim and Abu Dawud.

events.text: The passing of the Prophet ﷺ

hard.explain: The span in Common Era years, from the first revelation to the taking of Jerusalem under Umar.
The legislation of several pillars clustered in the second year after the Hijrah, with Badr falling in Ramadan of that year.
Five major scholars across four centuries. Al-Qurtubi and al-Nawawi died within four years of each other.
The later medieval scholars in sequence, ending with Ibn Hajar, author of the major commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari.
